newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks mixed amid continued disinterest.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks mixed amid continued disinterest.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in markets where the only strongly defined trend continued to be investor apathy, brokers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index saw 0.02 percent shaved off Wednesday's value as it closed at 13,605.79 on 729.1 million peso trading volume. Bogota's IBB index edged marginally up, ending the session 0.15 percent up at 869.8 on a total trade of 1.6 billion pesos.
"There was a slight upturn in volumes being traded, but in general terms prices and transactions are little changed," one Bogota broker said.

The main highlight on the Bogota exchange was a 553.75 million peso trade in Banco de Colombia shares, which ended 0.47 percent down at 418. More than 370 million pesos in insurance company Suramericana de Seguros changed hands at an unchanged price of 18,500 pesos.

"Banco de Colombia's situation is a little special because its share price rose in the expectation of this year's dividend and now it is dropping back to a more realistic level," the dealer added. "In terms of the Suramericana de Seguros deal it seems a foreign fund was buying up shares, and possibly the Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate too."

Some foreign funds seem to believe that Colombian stocks are undervalued compared to other markets in the region. In other deals of the day, Banco Industrial Colombiano rose 0.17 percent to 3,506 on a total trade of 183 million pesos and brewing giant Bavaria drifted up 0.14 percent to close at 4,008 on a 288 million peso volume.

"There's a lot of demand for Bavaria given how thin overall demand is and that has nudged prices up a bit," another Bogota broker said. The main movers in Medellin were Banco Industrial Colombiano, stable at 3,510 pesos on a 211.3 million peso volume, and Bavaria, up 0.12 percent to 4,005.
